record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Classify all surjective quadratic stochastic operators on the simplex S^{m-1} in every dimension m >= 5.

evidence.quote: In [5] and [28] a description of surjective QSOs defined on S m−1 for m = 2, 3, 4 and classification of extreme points of the set of such operators are given.
Problem 14. Describe the set of all surjective QSOs defined on S m−1 for any m ≥ 5.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $m\ge 2$ and let $S^{m-1}=\{x=(x_1,\dots,x_m)\in\mathbb{R}^m: x_i\ge 0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i=1\}$ denote the standard $(m-1)$-dimensional simplex. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) on $S^{m-1}$ is a map $V:S^{m-1}\to S^{m-1}$ of the form
$$(Vx)_k=\sum_{i,j=1}^m p_{ij,k}\,x_i x_j,\qquad k=1,\dots,m,$$
where the coefficients $\{p_{ij,k}\}$ satisfy
$$p_{ij,k}=p_{ji,k}\ge 0\quad\text{for all }i,j,k,\qquad \sum_{k=1}^m p_{ij,k}=1\quad\text{for all }i,j.$$
The QSO $V$ is called surjective if $V(S^{m-1})=S^{m-1}$.

For every dimension $m\ge 5$, give a complete description (classification) of the set of all surjective quadratic stochastic operators on $S^{m-1}$, including a description of the extreme points of this set.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work by Mukhamedov and collaborators established that a quadratic stochastic operator on the finite-dimensional simplex $S^{m-1}$ is surjective if and only if it is orthogonal-preserving, and provided a full description of such operators for arbitrary $m$ (showing equivalently that surjectivity is equivalent to bijectivity, and that every such operator has the form $Q(x)=\Pi V(x)$ for a permutation matrix $\Pi$ and a Lotka–Volterra QSO $V$). This appears to resolve the classification problem for all $m\ge 5$.

status_evidence.title: On the surjectivity of quadratic stochastic operators acting on the simplex
status_evidence.snippet: A quadratic stochastic operator associated with a cubic stochastic matrix is a surjection of the simplex if and only if it is bijective, and all surjective quadratic stochastic operators of the simplex have been described.
status_evidence.claim: The classification of surjective QSOs on S^{m-1} for general m has been obtained, with surjectivity equivalent to bijectivity (and to the orthogonal-preserving property).

status_evidence.title: Orthogonal-preserving and surjective cubic stochastic operators
status_evidence.snippet: For QSOs, surjectivity is equivalent to the orthogonal-preserving property; analogous results are extended to cubic stochastic operators.
status_evidence.claim: The quadratic case is settled and used as the basis for analogous results in higher-degree (cubic) stochastic operators.
